rows.name: Burry Port
rows.description: Near head of West pier while 10 feet water

rows.name: Saundersfoot, South Pier
rows.description: One fixed red light or yellow ball while 8 feet

rows.name: Tenby Pier Head
rows.description: One fixed red Tide light for steamers, &c.

rows.name: CALDY ISLAND
rows.character: One occulting bright or red light, ½ min.
rows.description: White tower, 52 ft. high, on S. part of island. Light eclipsed for 3 secs., once in every ½ minute; bright seaward; red towards Old Castle Head, from W. by N. ¾ N. to N.W. by W., and over Woolhouse Shoal from N. by E. ½ E. to N.E. ¾ E.

rows.name: MILFORD HAVEN ST. ANN'S POINT
rows.description: White towers, 75 and 42 ft. high, 610 ft. apart, on W. side. In line, N.N.W., lead in clear of Crow and Toes Rocks. A red ray from high lighthouse shows over Chapel and Harbour Rocks between S.E. and East.

rows.name: Great Castle Head
rows.description: In line, N.E. by E. ½ E., lead in mid-channel between St. Ann's Point & Mid-channel Rock

rows.name: Pembroke Dockyard
rows.description: In line, S.E. by E. ½ E., lead up. High light shown betw. W. by N. ¾ N. and N.W. ½ N. Low light betw. W. by N. ½ N. and N.N.E.; a green sector is shown over Carr Spit betw. N. ½ W. and N. by W. ½ W.

rows.name: Neyland Pier
rows.description: A fix. br. floating lt. off end of landing-pier... Bright leading lights shown for G. W. R. Co.'s vessels, two at Neyland Point and two at Hazelbeach, to clear shoal ground off Weare Point and Neyland Spit. Shown from huts, painted red and white.

rows.name: SMALLS
rows.character: One occulting bright or red light, 1 min.
rows.description: Granite tower, 141 ft. high, red & white bands. Light eclipsed twice in quick succession, followed by 54 secs. light; bright seaward; red over Hats and Barrels Rocks between E. ½ S. and S.E. ¾ E.

rows.name: SOUTH BISHOP ROCK
rows.description: White tower, 36 ft. high

rows.name: New Quay
rows.character: One fix. bright or red lt.
rows.description: On pier-head, September 15 to March 12. To southward of E. ½ N. the light is red

rows.name: CARDIGAN BAY LT.-V.
rows.character: One rev. red lt., ½ min.
rows.description: In 35 fathoms, at 20 miles N. by W. from Port Cardigan

rows.name: Aberystwith
rows.character: 1. One fix. br. or red lt. 2. Two fix. br. Tide lts.
rows.description: 1. On pier-head; light red to South and West, bright to W.N.W. and N.N.E. 2. Two lights in a field, over inner end of harbour, while sufficient water

rows.name: ST. TUDWALL ROADS
rows.character: 1. One occulting bright or red light 2. One lower fix. red lt.
rows.description: 1. White tower, 35 feet high, on West island. Light vis. 8 secs., eclipsed 2 secs.; bright to westward betw. N. by E. and S. by W.; thence red to S.E.; thence br. to N.E. by E. ½ E., and thence red to N. by E. Obscured by East Island betw. N.E. ½ E. & E. by N. ½ N. 2. A red ray, with an arc of 15°, is shown over Carreg-y-trai, from E. by S. to E. ½ N., from window 16 ft. below main light

rows.name: BARDSEY ISLAND
rows.character: One occult. br. lt., ½ min.
rows.description: A square white tower, 99 feet high. Light eclipsed for 3 secs. once in every ½ minute...

rows.name: Llanddwyn Island
rows.description: Visible between N.W. ½ N. and S.W. ¾ W.

rows.name: Carnarvon
rows.description: One fixed red light on pier-head

rows.name: Gwydir
rows.description: Fixed lt. on pier; red seaward, br. N. of N.E.

rows.name: CARNARVON BAY LT.-V.
rows.description: In 30 fathoms, at 12¾ miles S.W. by S. ½ S. from South Stack lt.-ho. Flashes bright, bright, and red. Red, with small ball over large one

rows.name: SOUTH STACK ROCK
rows.description: White tower, 84 ft. high. During fogs a smaller bright revolving light, 1 minute, at 90 ft., is shown at 65 yards W. by S. of lighthouse, between S. ½ W. and N.E. ¾ E. (In partial fogs the two revolving lights may appear as one irregular light)

rows.name: Holyhead
rows.character: 1. One flash. red lt., 7½ s. 2. One fixed bright lt. 3. One small red light 4. Fix. red and green lts.
rows.description: 1. Lighthouse on breakwater. Fixed lt. visible between flashes, within 3 or 4 miles. 2. On end of wooden jetty; old harbour 3. On old pier-head; shown from N.E. ½ N. to N.E. by N. ½ N., to clear Platters, &c. 4. Red light on North side, green light on South side, of inner harbour
